articles.originalTitle: Julia Stoschek Foundation to reopen Düsseldorf headquarters in 2027 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Julia Stoschek Foundation to Reopen Düsseldorf Headquarters in 2027
articles.excerpt: A month after closing its Berlin exhibition space, the Julia Stoschek Foundation announced it will reopen its Düsseldorf headquarters in April 2027 following renovations.
articles.content: Following the closure of its Berlin exhibition space in October, the nonprofit Julia Stoschek Foundation announced it will reopen its Düsseldorf headquarters in April 2027. The Düsseldorf space had closed for renovation in 2025. The inaugural exhibition in the revamped venue will feature works by 43 artists drawn from the foundation's collection, which focuses primarily on time-based art. Founder Julia Stoschek expressed joy at the collection's growth, noting that the Berlin location operated for 10 years before its closure as part of a strategic realignment. The reopening in Düsseldorf coincides with the foundation's 20th anniversary. Titled Selfish in Bed, the inaugural exhibition takes its name from a work by Sarah Lucas and will run from April 2027 to December 2027. It will include pieces by artists such as Wolfgang Tillmans, Bill Viola, Simon Fujiwara, Rosemarie Trockel, and Tracey Emin.

articles.originalTitle: 2026 Record Awards Winner: The Snake Building by C+S Architects - Architectural Record
articles.title: C+S Architects Wins Award for The Snake Building in Belgium
articles.excerpt: Located on a former industrial site in Aarschot, Belgium, the 29-unit residential project The Snake Building has been recognized in the 2026 Record Awards.
articles.content: Constructed as part of a regeneration scheme for a former industrial site in the historic Belgian city of Aarschot, a multifamily housing project has been completed. Designed by C+S Architects, the four-story development rises from a J-shaped lot and contains 29 residential units within a master plan led by a2o Architekten. The massing consists of five gabled volumes separated by alley-like gaps that accommodate balconies, creating an arrangement that resembles a typical Flemish streetscape. The facade features hand-laid long-format gray bricks punctured by timber-framed windows. A rear courtyard provides exposure for terraces while facilitating daylighting and ventilation. The street-facing elevations are wrapped by a landscaped plaza featuring ground-level retail storefronts, complemented by a below-grade parking garage for residents.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Examines the Dual Imperial History of Istanbul
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum has released an exhibition guide exploring the rich artistic traditions and historical evolution of Constantinople and Istanbul across two empires.
articles.content: Tracing the history of the city from Constantinople to Istanbul, the settlement was established as a capital when Roman Emperor Constantine I designated Byzantion as Nova Roma in 330 CE. Situated at the meeting point of Asia and Europe, the city served as the center of the Byzantine Empire until its fall in 1453, and subsequently as the Ottoman capital until 1922. A large print exhibition guide published by the Victoria and Albert Museum explores the architectural achievements and contrasting artistic traditions of the metropolis. While Byzantine Constantinople emphasized sacred images such as Christ Pantocrator in public and religious spaces, the Ottoman tradition favored text and calligraphy. The city's security relied on engineering feats including the 5.6-kilometer Theodosian Walls and the Aqueduct of Valens. Objects featured in the related research include ivory plaques, illuminated manuscripts, and precious stone cameos, illustrating the cosmopolitan fabric and diverse religious heritage preserved across sixteen centuries of imperial history.

articles.originalTitle: As war continues, local people mobilise to salvage southern Lebanon’s history - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Local People in Southern Lebanon Mobilise to Save History Amid Continuing War
articles.excerpt: As regional heritage sites and villages face destruction amid ongoing conflict, local officials, artists and residents are striving to document and preserve what remains.
articles.content: Ongoing conflict and occupation in southern Lebanon continue to threaten the region's historical fabric and cultural heritage. As homes, cemeteries, olive groves and monuments suffer destruction across villages, residents and officials are attempting salvage efforts. Riad Al-Assaad, speaking from Zrariyeh, notes that buildings have been levelled while people work to protect their historical existence. UNESCO-protected castles and heritage sites have also been impacted by the hostilities. Ali Badawi, the culture ministry's regional director, states that teams cannot access occupied locations and must rely on satellite imagery and military footage. Joanne Farchakh Bajjaly, founder of the heritage organisation Biladi, reports widespread destruction of historical structures, religious sites, cemeteries and trees. Artist Oussama Baalbaki describes how his family home in Odaisseh was destroyed with explosives, severing their connection to ancestral land. Experts and officials emphasize that restoration projects remain on hold as hostilities persist across the south.

articles.originalTitle: jean nouvel’s shenzhen opera house takes shape on the waterfront, with completion set for 2028 - Designboom
articles.title: Ateliers Jean Nouvel Designed Shenzhen Opera House Scheduled for Completion in 2028
articles.excerpt: Designed by Ateliers Jean Nouvel, the Shenzhen Opera House is taking shape along the Shekou waterfront in China. Titled Light of the Sea, the project is scheduled for completion in December 2028 with a background noise rating target below NR 15.
articles.content: Designed by Ateliers Jean Nouvel, the Shenzhen Opera House is under construction along the Shekou waterfront in Shenzhen, China. Titled Light of the Sea, the cultural complex is organized around a fluid roof and features four performance venues, including a 2,100-seat opera hall, an 1,800-seat concert hall, a 1,000-seat small opera hall, and a 500-seat multifunctional theater. The architectural program also integrates public facilities, a production center, artist accommodations, and offices. The design proposes a sweeping curved roof evoking ocean waves, while the interior auditorium incorporates mother-of-pearl finishes on acoustic surfaces. The project targets a background noise rating below NR 15 to meet strict acoustic requirements. Construction is progressing with the main roof structure scheduled for completion in 2027, and the overall cultural complex slated for delivery in December 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Showcases Digital Art and Contemporary Masterpieces
articles.excerpt: Taking place at a cultural crossroads in the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach unites voices in contemporary art while highlighting new frontiers in digital creations.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach presents a program that unites prominent voices in contemporary art alongside innovative presentations. The regional art fair brings together modern masterpieces and emerging talent on a single platform. The Zero 10 platform, dedicated to digital-era art, returns with Generation, its largest presentation to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, the exhibition spans 19 projects and explores connections between digital technologies and traditional art forms. Encompassing algorithmic art, immersive environments, painting, sculpture, and textiles, the presentation highlights works by creators such as Sarah Meyohas, Jon Rafman, and Studio Drift. Refik Anadol's collaboration with the Yawanawá community transforms Amazonian artwork, music, and weather data into evolving digital imagery. Meanwhile, Harm van den Dorpel draws on historical geometric drawings to produce generative pieces that unfold in real time during the event.

articles.originalTitle: Sumayya Vally Unveils First Permanent UAE Project With Dubai’s Elie Khouri Art Foundation - ArchDaily
articles.title: Sumayya Vally to Design Permanent Home for Elie Khouri Art Foundation in Dubai
articles.excerpt: Sumayya Vally of Counterspace will transform a villa in Dubai's Jumeirah 1 district into the permanent home for the Elie Khouri Art Foundation, featuring galleries, education, and public spaces ahead of a late 2028 opening.
articles.content: The Elie Khouri Art Foundation has appointed Sumayya Vally of Counterspace to design its permanent home in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Scheduled to open in late 2028, the institution will occupy a repurposed villa in the Jumeirah 1 district, transforming the residential property into a venue for contemporary art exhibitions, education, and public programming. Vally will lead the architectural transformation, incorporating galleries, educational spaces, pavilions, a garden, and hospitality areas while retaining the site's domestic character. The architectural concept draws spatial references from the street architecture of Beirut and the inward-facing organization of traditional Gulf courtyard houses, using the existing villa's architectural features to inform a contemporary language. Founded by French-Lebanese art collector and philanthropist Elie Khouri, the foundation builds on over two decades of collecting. Directed by Caroline Louca, the institution plans to bring together works from its collection, temporary exhibitions, and learning initiatives to engage a broader public with contemporary art practices.

articles.originalTitle: Museum Organizations Call Bipartisan Infrastruture Bill a ‘Sweeping Assault’ on Historic and Sacred Places - ARTnews.com
articles.title: US Senate Advances Infrastructure Bill While Preservation Groups Condemn Measure
articles.excerpt: A newly advanced US Senate infrastructure bill has sparked strong opposition from museums and preservationists who argue it severely weakens protections for historic and sacred sites.
articles.content: The US Senate advanced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 by a vote of 73 to 25. Introduced by Senator Shelley Moore Capito, the 500-page bill aims to reduce permitting delays for infrastructure and energy projects. Proponents argued that regulatory bottlenecks cost manufacturers 12.1 billion dollars annually and lock up 1.8 trillion dollars in investments nationwide. However, the legislation faced immediate backlash from historic preservationists and museum organizations. Approximately 800 demonstrators gathered at the US Capitol to protest the measure. Critics noted that the bill narrows the scope of the National Historic Preservation Act, makes tribal consultations optional, and removes public notification mandates for historic sites. A coalition representing over 1,200 organizations and tribal nations sent a formal letter to Congress demanding the defeat of the bill, characterizing it as a sweeping assault on federal protections enacted six decades ago for sacred and historic locations across the country.

articles.originalTitle: Italian Design Firm Henge Expands Into Tableware, Fragrances - WWD
articles.title: Italian Design Firm Henge Expands Into Tableware and Fragrances
articles.excerpt: Milan-based luxury furniture firm Henge has introduced its first collection of tableware, glassware, and home fragrances crafted from stone, glass, and metal.
articles.content: Italian luxury furniture maker Henge has expanded its portfolio into tableware, glassware, and home fragrances. The Milan-based company announced that its debut home collection relies on core materials such as stone, glass, and metal, featuring natural textures and hues. The collection includes Murano glass tumblers and a carafe designed by Ugo Cacciatori, alongside cast silver and gold trays by Yabu Pushelberg. Handcrafted in Carrara from Rouge Languedoc, Napoléon, and Gris Cévenol marbles, the Rever plates derive their name from the French word for dreaming. The brand also made its first foray into home fragrances with Henge Fragrance #34, named after its showroom at 34 Via della Spiga in Milan. The scent blends Calabrian bergamot, Sicilian lemon, and jasmine with notes of frankincense, Virginia tobacco, and Russian leather. This expansion aligns with an industry trend where high-end Italian design firms, including Molteni & C and Cassina, introduce smaller, more accessible design objects.

articles.originalTitle: London-Based Interior Designer Tala Fustok Introduces First Furniture Collection - WWD
articles.title: Interior Designer Tala Fustok Introduces First Furniture Collection
articles.excerpt: London-based interior designer Tala Fustok has announced her first furniture and accessory collection titled "Pieces" under her eponymous studio, noting that the new range reflects her life between London and Italy.
articles.content: London-based interior designer Tala Fustok has introduced her first furniture and accessory collection named "Pieces." Known for upscale residential projects and hotels such as The Mandrake, the Anglo-Palestinian designer stated that the new in-house range reflects her relaxed approach to living and her time divided between London and Apulia, Italy. The collection follows years of bespoke work and Fustok's redesign of her own Victorian home in Notting Hill. The "Pieces" lineup includes "Nest," an enveloping chenille-velvet bed designed for face-to-face conversation; "Lazy Sunday," an oversize sofa made for unwinding; and modular stainless-steel blocks that function as pedestals, coffee tables, or laptop stands. Available through the studio's website, clients can customize items using the firm's fabric archive, while the team facilitates delivery with international project experience. Fustok notes potential in hospitality, though her team is balancing pricing and quality for designs crafted by artisans in the U.K. and Italy. She is also developing artisan-made objects in southern Italy and designing a future lighting collection.

articles.originalTitle: Mexico is undergoing an architecture renaissance inspired by its ancient past - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Contemporary Mexican Architecture Draws Fresh Inspiration From Ancient Mesoamerican Roots
articles.excerpt: Writer and curator Su Wu examines the re-emergence of ancient Mesoamerican forms, motifs, and spatial principles in contemporary residential architecture across Mexico.
articles.content: A new generation of architects in Mexico is shaping a distinct design language by reinterpreting the construction principles of ancient Aztec, Maya, and other Mesoamerican peoples. A new book by writer and curator Su Wu documents how these ancient ideas are manifesting within private residential projects across the country. While Mesoamerican motifs previously appeared in large cultural institutions, their integration into private homes marks a shift toward deeply personal architectural efforts. Among the featured projects are Fernanda Canales's geometrically precise Casa 720 and Casa Bernal by Marcos Ruiz and Emmanuel Picault, which is oriented in relation to the Peña de Bernal monolith. Additional residential works highlighted include Juan O’Gorman's home for composer Conlon Nancarrow and a project by Pedro Reyes and Carla Fernández. Furthermore, artist Geraz Ato's hand-carved dwelling near Teotihuacán incorporates iconography and migration scenes referencing the region's ancient past. These residences demonstrate that Mesoamerican design principles remain relevant and active within contemporary private architecture.

articles.originalTitle: Getty Pitches In on First-Ever Conservation of an Earthquake-Damaged 17th-Century Church in the Andean Highlands of Peru - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Getty to Assist in First Conservation of Damaged Peruvian Church
articles.excerpt: The Getty is partnering with local authorities to undertake the first-ever conservation project on the 17th-century Church of Santo Tomás de Aquino in Peru's Cusco region.
articles.content: The Getty is working with local authorities on the first-ever conservation project for the 17th-century earthen Church of Santo Tomás de Aquino, located in the Andean highlands of Peru's Cusco region. The Peruvian government has allocated $5 million to a multi-year initiative to strengthen the earthquake-damaged structure and safeguard its collection of over 300 cultural objects, including 17th- and 18th-century paintings, gilded wooden retablos, and textiles. Construction is set to begin in 2027, utilizing the Getty Conservation Institute's Seismic Retrofitting Project methodologies. Among the notable works in the collection is a series of eight large easel paintings by Italian Jesuit artist Bernardo Bitti, created in Cusco in the late 1590s and previously thought to be lost. One painting from the series, "La Oración en el huerto," will be transferred to the Getty in 2027 for scientific analysis and conservation treatment. Experts note that the collection offers a rare research opportunity because it shows no evidence of prior restoration.

articles.originalTitle: Scholar Dishes About Finding a Long-Lost Caravaggio Painting in Paris - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Lost Caravaggio Painting Discovered in a Paris Gallery
articles.excerpt: Art historian Maria Cristina Terzaghi has shared details regarding a lost Caravaggio painting she identified in Paris.
articles.content: Art historian Maria Cristina Terzaghi has identified a painting missing for nearly two centuries in a Paris gallery as an original work by Caravaggio. Writing in La Repubblica, the Roma Tre University professor detailed her attribution of Young Man with a Carafe of Roses, believed to be painted in the 1590s. The composition features a young man alongside fruit and a water-filled glass carafe, with four earlier copies known to exist internationally. According to Terzaghi, the canvas appeared in a 1607 inventory belonging to Giuseppe Cesari before entering the Borghese collection, where records trace it until 1831. The trail later resumed in 1909 when a Paris bookseller's widow put the work up for auction as an anonymous piece. Terzaghi bases her authenticity claims on the quality of the subject's expressive face, the fabric, and the rendering of light through the glass carafe, comparing the floral details to descriptions by contemporary rival Giovanni Baglione. Questions remain regarding how the artwork traveled to Italy from France, and other specialists are expected to review the evidence. Meanwhile, another Italian art historian recently attributed a different portrait to Caravaggio.

articles.originalTitle: Oshinówò Studio tops Lutyens-designed war memorial with glass prism to honour Sierra Leone's Carrier Corps - Dezeen
articles.title: Oshinówò Studio Tops Lutyens-Designed War Memorial With Glass Prism in Freetown
articles.excerpt: The Commonwealth War Graves Commission unveiled a memorial to the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps in Freetown, featuring a structural glass pyramid by Oshinówò Studio placed atop a 1931 war memorial designed by Edwin Lutyens.
articles.content: The Commonwealth War Graves Commission unveiled a memorial to the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps in Freetown, Sierra Leone. Designed by Oshinówò Studio, the new structure sits atop a war memorial originally designed by British architect Edwin Lutyens in 1931. While the 1931 memorial honoured first world war soldiers, it omitted the names of the 946 members of the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps who died transporting supplies and materials. Oshinówò Studio extended the stone memorial by adding a structural glass pyramid etched with the names of the Carrier Corps men. According to founder Tosin Oshinówò, the new monument follows the existing tapering geometry, elevating the names etched into glass. Placing the Carrier Corps names higher than the soldiers served as a symbolic gesture in which the corps members are symbolically carried by their comrades. The project also incorporates a laser beacon visible from up to 5 kilometres on significant days of remembrance. Furthermore, stonemasons and bronze specialists from the Commonwealth War Graves Commission fully restored the 1930s memorial during the project.

articles.originalTitle: Matteo Thun designs Torre Velasca interiors using “the building itself as the starting point” - Dezeen
articles.title: Matteo Thun Designs New Interiors for Milan’s Iconic Torre Velasca
articles.excerpt: Italian architect Matteo Thun has designed 72 apartment interiors in the upper floors of Milan’s Torre Velasca, drawing direct inspiration from the building's original materials and colors.
articles.content: Italian architect Matteo Thun has completed the interior design of 72 apartments ranging from suites to duplex penthouses in the upper floors of the historic tower. Built in the 1950s by architecture studio BBPR, the skyscraper project focused on reinterpretation, using the original materials and colors of the structure as a starting point. The studio preserved original details such as doors, window frames, loggias, and tiles in kitchens and bathrooms, pairing them with evergreen design classics and custom furniture. Custom pale pink velvet wall coverings by textile company Dedar echo the hue of the tower's specialized facade plaster. Darker gradations of the building's original blue and green floor tiles define the entrance areas and bedrooms. Alongside the apartments, Thun designed the reception, lobby, and ground-floor corridors. The architect noted that working with such a distinctive structure challenged the team to ensure the original character remained relevant today while staying true to the original vision.

articles.originalTitle: Edgar Degas | Promenade beside the Sea | L819 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Edgar Degas Painting Promenade beside the Sea at The National Gallery
articles.excerpt: Edgar Degas's oil sketch Promenade beside the Sea, created around 1860, is housed at The National Gallery in London. The work depicts an elegantly attired couple on horseback along the coast of the Bay of Naples.
articles.content: Held at The National Gallery in London, Promenade beside the Sea by Edgar Degas is an early example of the horse and rider theme the artist explored throughout his career. Produced around 1860, the oil sketch depicts an elegantly attired gentleman in black and a lady in a dark riding habit riding along the coast beneath cliffs as the sun sets. The location corresponds to the Bay of Naples, an area Degas visited during family trips. Although it appears to be a rapid outdoor study, the composition was likely produced in the studio using earlier preparatory studies, with the left-hand section of the riders based on a notebook sketch in Paris. Measuring 22.5 by 32.5 cm, the oil on canvas is part of the Gere Collection on long-term loan to the gallery and is displayed in Room 39. Painted shortly after Degas established his first studio in Paris and years before the Impressionist movement, the artwork demonstrates his lifelong interest in capturing equine movement and motion through open brushwork.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Explores Byzantine and Ottoman Legacy in Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is presenting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition spanning the period from AD 330 to 1922. The exhibition examines the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, highlighting their creative legacy that shaped the Mediterranean and beyond. Spread across four main sections, the exhibition features over 200 objects, including rare decorative arts, fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The first section, Roman Beginnings, explores the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire under Constantine the Great, focusing on its infrastructure and the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth, the second section, explores how art and architecture served Christianity. Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials, while the final section, Life in the City, investigates the city's cosmopolitan character, religious coexistence, and 19th-century shifts in style. The exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Best Government/Public Building: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Morocco Pavilion: DECLOSION - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale 2026 Morocco Pavilion Announces Declosion Performance
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for the Arsenale during the 2026 Venice Biennale, the Morocco Pavilion will present the performance Declosion, drawing on the cosmology of Hesiod's Theogony.
articles.content: As part of the 2026 Venice Biennale, the Morocco Pavilion at the Arsenale will host the performance titled Declosion. Drawing from the chaos narrative in Hesiod's Theogony, the performance invokes Clotho, the figure who spins the thread of life. Engaging in a dialogue with Amina Agueznay's artwork, the event explores the cyclical rhythm of existence spanning birth, life, and death. Featuring performer Inès Abergel within the installation Asǝṭṭa, the work reveals the transition from emptiness to fullness and nonbeing to being. Artistic support for the performance is provided by Amina Agueznay, with music composition by Guilain Delanoue. Movement advisors include Alice Dardenne and Romane Piffaut, while scenography is advised by Amine Slimani and Federico Urso. Objects for the installation are crafted by Malika Benmoumen, Mahdia Anoufr, Koltoum Gaddem, Khaddouj Alja, and Florian SôngNguyen. The performance is scheduled for November 21, 2026, from 16:30 to 16:50.

articles.originalTitle: Enthusiasm Remains High as Dubai Design Week and Design Doha Biennale Kick Off - WWD
articles.title: Dubai Design Week and Design Doha Biennial Kick Off
articles.excerpt: Despite regional challenges, Dubai Design Week and the Design Doha Biennial 2026 are launching with participants from over 50 countries, celebrating creativity and regional heritage.
articles.content: Despite regional challenges affecting trade, creative enthusiasm remains strong as Dubai Design Week opens its doors through November 8, featuring participants from over 50 countries. Anchored by the UAE Designer Exhibition under the theme Inherited Futures and curated by architect AlZaina Lootah, the event explores how inherited materials and rituals intersect with contemporary design. Key highlights include a collaboration between Yinka Ilori and Veuve Clicquot, Luke Edward Hall's immersive silverware experience for Buccellati, and workshops hosted by MillerKnoll. Additionally, designer Tristan Auer delivers the opening keynote following his appointment to lead the Burj Al Arab restoration, while Molteni&C inaugurates a new flagship on Jumeirah Beach Road. Opening Thursday, the Design Doha Biennial 2026 presents over 15 exhibitions featuring creators from the MENASA region and beyond. Fromm.Lab showcases 12 projects reinterpreting Arab heritage through contemporary design, and the Design Doha Prize announces winners across categories on November 7 at the Museum of Islamic Art, with an international jury led by India Mahdavi.

articles.originalTitle: Drop-in Design: Your Future City - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Designing the Future City Workshop at the V&A Museum
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum invites families and children aged 5 and over to design future public buildings using recycled materials in a free workshop.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a hands-on town planning event for children and families in collaboration with architectural designer Jahba Anan and RIBA. At the V&A South Kensington, participants will imagine and redesign how schools, hospitals, libraries, and train stations might look in 2050. Drawing inspiration from the Design 1900–Now galleries, the program allows visitors to examine how design has transformed daily life over the past 125 years. Supported by the Adobe Foundation, attendees will use recycled materials to build mini models of their dream buildings and contribute them to a growing city model over five days. The free drop-in event is suitable for ages 5 and above, with all materials provided on-site. Visitors must ensure children are attended at all times. The venue offers comprehensive accessibility features, including baby-changing facilities, quiet spaces, and ear defenders available upon request from the Learning Centre Desk for families requiring sensory support.

articles.originalTitle: Human Unreadable Act III by Operator - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Operator Duo Livestreams Act Three of Human Unreadable at the V&A
articles.excerpt: Artist duo Operator brings the final act of their Human Unreadable series, examining human and machine agency, to the Victoria and Albert Museum.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a livestream screening of Act III, the final act of the three-part work Human Unreadable by artist duo Operator, on 22 November 2026. Transmitted live from the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York, the multimedia performance examines negotiations between the body, ambition, and technology. The presentation utilizes 100 dance sequences from the Human Unreadable collection, woven together through scripted dialogue, performance art, lighting, scenic design, and an original score. Broadcast across multiple venues, the transmission features real-time editing from multiple camera perspectives. Commissioned by the Whitney Museum of American Art, the event forms part of the museum's digital art season exploring boundaries between human and machine agency.

articles.originalTitle: HISTORICAL ARCHIVE | The Pillar and the Ground of Truth by Pavel A. Florenskij - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale to Host Lecture and Performance Series on Pavel A. Florensky
articles.excerpt: The Historical Archive of La Biennale di Venezia will present a five-evening special project dedicated to the thought of Pavel A. Florensky, directed by Antonello Pocetti.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia is presenting The Pillar and the Ground of Truth by Pavel A. Florensky as a special project of the Historical Archive within the Biennale of the Word. Taking place from 16 to 20 November at the Historical Archive's new premises at the Arsenale, the project is conceived and directed by Antonello Pocetti and comprises five evenings exploring Florensky's thought. Each evening features contributions from cultural and philosophical figures, followed by staged readings adapted from the author's writings. Tickets are available for 15 euros for full price, while five-evening subscriptions cost 60 euros. Student and under-26 tickets are priced at 10 euros, with 40 euros for subscriptions. Born in Yevlakh in 1882, Florensky studied mathematics before turning to philosophy and theology, and was ordained as a Russian Orthodox priest in 1911. Following the 1917 Revolution, he remained in Russia, where he participated in scientific projects before being arrested on counter-revolutionary charges and executed near Leningrad on 8 December 1937. The project highlights the Historical Archive as an active centre for cultural research, bringing memory into dialogue with the present.

articles.originalTitle: HISTORICAL ARCHIVE | The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florenskij - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Stages Pavel A. Florensky Project at Historical Archive
articles.excerpt: The Historical Archive of La Biennale di Venezia will present a five-day special project dedicated to Pavel A. Florensky, exploring the relationship between language and truth. The performances will take place from 16 to 20 November at the Arsenale.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia is presenting The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florensky as part of the Biennale of the Word. Taking place from 16 to 20 November 2026 at the new premises of the Historical Archive at the Arsenale, the project is conceived and directed by Antonello Pocetti across five evenings. The texts have been adapted from Florensky's writings to convey the depth of his reflections. Each evening opens with contributions from figures in culture, philosophy, and religion, followed by staged readings. Born in 1882 in Yevlakh, Azerbaijan, Florensky studied mathematics in Moscow before turning to philosophy and theology. Ordained an Orthodox priest in 1911, he engaged in research spanning mathematics, music, painting, and philosophy. Following the 1917 Revolution, he remained in Russia, where he participated in scientific projects before being arrested on counter-revolutionary charges and executed near Leningrad on 8 December 1937. Tickets become available starting 29 October on the La Biennale di Venezia website.
